name: program
meaning: A set of instructions for a computer to follow.
example: A program can add two prices and show the total.

name: code
meaning: Instructions written in a programming language.
example: Code can tell a computer to display a greeting. Each language has its own spelling for that instruction.

name: value
meaning: One piece of information that code can use.
example: 5 is a number value. "Hello" is a text value.

name: variable
meaning: A name that lets your code use a value.
example: A variable named score can hold 5, then be updated to hold 8.

name: string
meaning: Text stored as a value. Quotes mark where the text starts and ends.
example: "Hello" is a string. 5 is a number, but "5" is text.

name: integer
meaning: A number with no fractional part. It can be negative, zero, or positive.

name: floating-point number
meaning: A number type that can hold a fractional part. Some values are only approximate.
example: A price like 2.5 can be stored as a floating-point number.

name: Boolean
meaning: A value with just two choices: true or false.
example: The question “Is 5 greater than 3?” has the Boolean answer true.

name: function
meaning: A reusable block of code that can receive inputs, perform a task, and give back a result. Functions can have names or be unnamed.
example: A function can add two numbers each time the program asks it to run.

name: function call
meaning: An instruction that asks a function to run.
example: Calling a greeting function asks it to produce a greeting now.

name: parameter
meaning: A name in a function definition that stands for an input.
example: A greeting function can define a parameter named name for the person to greet.

name: argument
meaning: A value you give a function when you call it.
example: Supplying the name Mina to a greeting function passes Mina as its argument.

name: return value
meaning: The result a function gives back to the code that called it.
example: A function that adds 2 and 3 can return 5. Returning is not the same as printing.

name: method
meaning: A function that belongs to an object or type.
example: A text value can have a method that produces uppercase text; its name depends on the language.

name: expression
meaning: Code that produces a value.
example: 2 + 3 is an expression. Its value is 5.

name: statement
meaning: An instruction that tells the program to do something.
example: An assignment statement can store a new value in a score variable.

name: assignment
meaning: Giving a value to a name or another place that stores it.
example: Assigning 5 to score stores that value; it does not ask whether two values are equal.

name: operator
meaning: A symbol or word that performs an action on values.

name: comparison
meaning: A check of how values relate, such as whether they are equal.
example: 5 > 3 compares two numbers and gives true.

name: condition
meaning: A check used to decide what happens next.
example: A condition can ask whether a score is above 10 before choosing what to display.

name: branch
meaning: One path a program can take after a decision.
example: An if branch handles a true condition. An else branch handles the other case.

name: loop
meaning: Code that repeats instructions.
example: A loop can print each name in a list.

name: iteration
meaning: One pass through a loop, or the act of going through items.
example: Printing three list items takes three loop iterations.

name: list
meaning: An ordered collection of items.
example: A shopping list can hold book and pen as two ordered items. Code notation varies by language.

name: array
meaning: An ordered collection whose items can be reached by position.
example: An array can hold 10, 20 and 30 in order. Indexing rules depend on the language.

name: Collection index
meaning: A position used to find an item in an ordered collection. Many languages start at 0.
context: Position in a list, array, or similar collection. A database index is a different meaning of index.

name: Database index
meaning: An extra database structure that can help find rows faster. It takes space and must be updated when data changes.
example: An index on genre can speed up a search for books in one genre.
context: Database lookup structure, not an item’s position in an array.

name: dictionary
meaning: A collection that connects keys to values.
example: A dictionary can connect the key name to the value Mina.

name: key
meaning: A label used to find a value in a collection.
example: The key score can identify a stored value of 5.

name: tuple
meaning: An ordered group of values treated as one value. Exact type and mutability rules depend on the language.
example: A pair of values can represent a point with horizontal and vertical coordinates.

name: set
meaning: A Python collection with no duplicate items. It does not provide numbered positions.

name: object
meaning: A value that can have its own data and actions.
example: A player object might have a name, a score, and a method to add points.

name: property
meaning: A named piece of data or a setting that belongs to something.
example: A player object can expose a score property.

name: Class (object-oriented programming)
meaning: A definition used to create objects with shared kinds of data and behavior.
example: A Player class can create separate players, each with a score.
context: A programming type or template for objects. An HTML/CSS class is a different use of the word.

name: instance
meaning: One object created from a class or type.
example: Two Player objects are two separate instances of Player.

name: mutable
meaning: Able to be changed after it is made.
example: A mutable collection can accept another item without replacing the whole collection.

name: immutable
meaning: Not changeable after it is made. You can make a new value instead.
example: An immutable text value cannot be edited in place; an operation can produce a new text value instead.

name: scope
meaning: The part of a program where a name can be used.
example: A local name made inside a function is normally used inside that function.

name: closure
meaning: A function that keeps access to names from the place where it was created.
example: A counter function can remember its count between calls.

name: recursion
meaning: Solving a task by having a function call itself on smaller parts.
example: A folder search can search each folder inside the current folder.

name: base case
meaning: The stopping case in a recursive function.
example: A countdown can stop calling itself when the number reaches 0.

name: iterator
meaning: Something that gives you items one at a time and remembers its place.
example: Asking an iterator for its next item advances through a collection.

name: iterable
meaning: Something you can go through item by item.
example: An iterable collection lets a loop visit its items one by one.

name: generator
meaning: Code that produces items one at a time instead of preparing them all at once.
example: A generator can produce the next number only when it is requested.

name: syntax
meaning: The writing rules of a programming language.
example: Missing a required punctuation mark can cause a syntax error. The required marks depend on the language.

name: indentation
meaning: Spaces at the start of a line that make nesting visible. Some languages also use them to define blocks.
example: Indenting a block makes its structure easier to see; whether those spaces affect execution depends on the language.

name: parentheses
meaning: The curved marks ( and ). They group things or surround function inputs.
example: The expression (2 + 3) groups an addition inside parentheses.

name: comment
meaning: A note in code for people to read. The program does not run it as an instruction.
example: A comment can explain why a calculation rounds a result. Comment markers depend on the language.

name: output
meaning: Information a program produces or shows.
example: A greeting program can produce the output Hello.

name: input
meaning: Information given to a program or function.
example: The numbers 2 and 3 are inputs to a function that adds them.

name: bug
meaning: A mistake that makes a program behave differently from what you intended.
example: Using subtraction when you meant addition is a bug.

name: exception
meaning: A signal that something went wrong while code was running. Code may be able to handle it.
example: Trying to open a missing file can raise an exception.

name: validation
meaning: Checking that input follows the rules your program needs.
example: Before saving a score, check that it is a whole number from 0 to 100.

name: algorithm
meaning: A clear set of steps for solving a problem.
example: To find the largest number, compare each number with the largest seen so far.

name: callback
meaning: A function passed to other code so that code can call it when needed.
example: A button can call your callback when someone clicks it.

name: asynchronous
meaning: Work that can finish later, letting other work happen while you wait.
example: Loading a web page can happen while the app still responds to clicks.

name: await
meaning: Wait for an asynchronous result inside the current async function.
example: An asynchronous function can wait for requested data before using it, without blocking all unrelated work.

name: Promise
meaning: A JavaScript object for a result that may arrive later or fail.
example: A request for data can return a Promise before the data arrives.

name: state
meaning: The information an app currently remembers.
example: A counter that shows 3 has a current count state of 3.

name: event
meaning: Something that happens, such as a click, that code can respond to.
example: An input event tells your app that a field changed.

name: handler
meaning: A function that responds to an event or request.
example: A click handler can add one to a counter.

name: type
meaning: A category of value that tells code what operations make sense.
example: A number can be added. A string is text.

name: TypeScript interface
meaning: In TypeScript, a description of the properties an object should have.
example: A Player interface can require a text name and a numeric score.
context: This entry describes a TypeScript type contract. In everyday software discussion, interface can also mean a screen or a boundary between systems.

name: union type
meaning: A type that allows more than one choice.
example: string | number allows either text or a number.

name: type guard
meaning: A check that helps TypeScript narrow down what type a value has.
example: typeof value === "string" checks whether value is text.

name: generic
meaning: Code with a placeholder for a type so it can work with different types safely.
example: A collection can use a type placeholder, then accept a specific item type such as a number or text type.

name: destructure
meaning: Take named parts out of an object or array into separate names.
example: Separate the score and name from a player record into individual variables.

name: Text interpolation
meaning: Building text by inserting values from expressions. Each programming language has its own syntax for this.
example: Python: f"Hi {name}". JavaScript: `Hi ${name}`. Both insert name, but their quote marks and braces differ.
context: A JavaScript template literal and a Python f-string are related tools, not interchangeable syntax.

name: Swift protocol
meaning: In Swift, a list of requirements a type promises to provide.
example: A Transport protocol might require a description property.
context: This entry describes Swift type requirements. A network protocol instead specifies communication rules.

name: actor
meaning: In Swift, a type that helps protect its changing data when several tasks use it.
example: A store actor can keep two tasks from changing its data at the same time.

name: Swift optional
meaning: A Swift value that may contain a value or may contain nothing, written nil.
context: This entry describes Swift’s value-or-nil type, not merely an optional task.

name: component
meaning: A reusable piece of a user interface.
example: A Profile component can show a name and picture.

name: prop
meaning: An input passed to a React component.
example: In <Profile name="Mina" />, name is a prop.

name: render
meaning: Create the description or display of what the user should see.
example: A user interface renders a heading using the current name.

name: element
meaning: A piece of a web page, often written with a start tag, content, and an end tag.

name: attribute
meaning: A named setting on an HTML element, or a named member of an object in languages such as Python.
example: In , src is an HTML attribute.

name: selector
meaning: A CSS pattern that chooses which elements to style.
example: .card chooses elements with the class card.

name: HTML/CSS class
meaning: An HTML label used to group elements, often so CSS can style them.
example: class="card" lets the CSS selector .card choose that element.
context: A reusable label on HTML elements, not an object-oriented class definition.

name: accessibility
meaning: Making an app usable by people with different needs and ways of using a computer.
example: A button should work with a keyboard as well as a mouse.

name: API
meaning: An agreed way for one piece of software to ask another for data or actions.
example: A weather app can ask a weather API for a forecast.

name: API key
meaning: A secret value that identifies or authorizes an app when it uses a service.
example: Keep an API key out of shared source code and public web pages.

name: JSON
meaning: A text format for storing or sending structured data.

name: CSV
meaning: A text format for rows of data, often with commas between fields.
example: name,score is a header row. A later row might be Mina,5.

name: parse
meaning: Read text using rules so code can work with its structure.
example: A JSON parser can turn structured JSON text into values that code can use.

name: database
meaning: An organized place for storing and finding data.
example: A book database can store a title and author for each book.

name: SQL
meaning: A language used to work with data in relational databases.
example: SELECT title FROM books asks for book titles.

name: query
meaning: A request to find or work with data.
example: A query can ask for all books by one author.

name: row
meaning: One record in a table.
example: One row in a books table can describe one book.

name: column
meaning: One named kind of information in a table.
example: A title column holds the title for each book.

name: join
meaning: A database operation that combines matching information from tables.
example: Join orders to customers to show who placed each order.

name: SQL NULL
meaning: A marker for a missing or unknown database value.
example: NULL minutes means the minutes are unknown, not zero.
context: SQL uses three-valued logic for missing/unknown values. JavaScript null and Python None have different language rules.

name: transaction
meaning: A group of database changes handled as one unit: all succeed, or they can be undone together.
example: Moving 3 items between two counts should update both counts or neither.

name: CTE
meaning: A named query result used inside one larger SQL statement.
example: WITH totals AS (...) lets the following query use totals.

name: middleware
meaning: Code that runs as a request passes through a server, before it reaches its final handler.
example: Sign-in middleware can check who is making a request.

name: request
meaning: A message asking another program or server to do something.
example: GET /entries asks a server for saved entries.

name: response
meaning: The reply to a request.
example: A server response can contain data and a status such as 200.

name: authentication
meaning: Checking who someone is.
example: Signing in helps an app check your identity.

name: authorization
meaning: Checking what someone is allowed to do.
example: Being signed in does not mean you may edit another person’s notes.

name: terminal
meaning: A place to type commands for your computer.
example: Type a command in a terminal to build or run a local program.

name: dependency
meaning: Other code a project needs to work.
example: A project can depend on a library for reading CSV files.

name: Git
meaning: A tool that records versions of your files so you can review and recover changes.
example: A Git commit records a saved checkpoint of changes.

name: commit
meaning: In Git, a recorded checkpoint of changes with a message explaining them.
example: A commit named "Fix total" can record the corrected calculation.

name: constructor
meaning: Code used when creating an object to prepare its starting state.
example: Creating a player object can initialize its starting score.
context: Languages differ in how they allocate an object and initialize its starting state.

name: list comprehension
meaning: A short way to build a new Python list by going through other items.

name: modulo
meaning: The amount left after whole-number division.
example: 7 % 3 gives 1 because 7 is two groups of 3 with 1 left.

name: module
meaning: A file or unit of code that can share its functions and values with other code.
example: A helper module can make a function available to another part of a program.

name: import
meaning: Make code from another module available here.
example: An import can make a helper function from another module available in this file.

name: finite
meaning: A finite number is not positive or negative infinity, or NaN (not a number). Those special values are called non-finite.
example: 12 is finite. Infinity and NaN are not.

name: boundary
meaning: A limit, often the smallest or largest allowed value.
example: For scores from 0 to 100, test 0 and 100 as well as numbers outside those limits.

name: timeout
meaning: A limit on how long code will wait for something.
example: A two-second timeout stops waiting if a request takes longer than two seconds.

name: retry
meaning: Try an operation again after it fails.
example: Allowing two attempts means one first try and at most one retry.

name: prerequisite
meaning: Something that must happen before another task can start.
example: Reading a file is a prerequisite for counting the words inside it.

name: cycle
meaning: A chain that leads back to something already in the chain.
example: If A needs B first and B needs A first, neither task can begin.

name: normalize
meaning: Put data into a consistent form before using it.
example: Removing extra edge spaces makes "  Read  " become "Read".

name: schema
meaning: A description of how data is organized and what kinds of values are allowed.
example: A table schema can require a name column and a numeric score column.

name: aggregate
meaning: Combine several values into one summary.
example: Adding a group of numbers produces one total.

name: reducer
meaning: A function that uses the current state and an action to decide the next state.
example: A counter reducer can turn count 3 and an add action into count 4.

name: memoized
meaning: Keeping a calculation’s previous result so it can be reused when its inputs have not changed.
example: A saved search result can be reused when the list and search text stay the same.

name: payload
meaning: The useful data carried by a message or event.
example: An event named progress might carry the payload {percent: 50}.

name: keyword
meaning: A word with a special meaning in a programming language.
example: A language can reserve words for decisions, loops or returning a result.

name: token
meaning: A small unit with meaning. In code it might be a name or symbol; in AI text it may be a word or part of one. An access token is different: it is a secret used for access.
example: In code, the name print is one token. Do not share an access token.
context: The meaning depends on context: a code token, a model’s text token, and an access token are different things. An access token may be a credential; never paste one into public examples.

name: AI
meaning: Computer systems that perform tasks such as recognizing patterns or generating text. Their answers can be wrong.
example: An AI helper may suggest code. Run and check the code before trusting it.

name: AI model
meaning: A system trained on examples to produce predictions or responses.
example: A language model can suggest an explanation, but it may invent details.
context: AI model is the broad term. A language model, including a large language model (LLM), is one kind; not every AI model generates language.

name: prompt
meaning: An instruction or question given to an AI tool. A program can also use a prompt to ask a person for input.
example: An AI prompt could be: Explain this function in two short sentences.

name: Machine learning
meaning: Building models by using data to adjust how they respond, rather than hand-writing every decision rule.
example: A message sorter learns patterns from example messages.

name: Neural network
meaning: A model built from connected calculation units, often arranged in layers. Training adjusts numerical parameters.
example: An image model combines calculations across layers to propose a label.
context: The units are mathematical operations, not living brain cells.

name: Model training
meaning: Using data and a learning method to adjust a model’s parameters or learned structure.
example: Repeated examples help adjust a model’s prediction rule.
context: Using a fact in the current conversation is not by itself a training update.

name: Inference
meaning: Using a model to calculate an output from supplied input.
example: A trained model receives a new photo and proposes a label.
context: A system can use current context during inference without changing its trained parameters.

name: Model weight
meaning: An adjustable number that controls how an input contributes to a model calculation.
example: With input 3 and weight 2, that weighted contribution is 6.
context: An attention weight calculated for the current input is distinct from a stored training parameter.

name: Loss function
meaning: A rule that measures how poorly a prediction fits the chosen training goal, using a number.
example: A distance-based loss is smaller when a numerical prediction is closer to its target.
context: Lower loss under one rule does not guarantee truth, fairness, or success on every task.

name: Backpropagation
meaning: A method that works backward through a network’s calculations to compute how parameter changes affect loss.
example: After a prediction and loss calculation, backpropagation computes gradients for the parameters.
context: Computing gradients and applying an optimizer update are separate steps.

name: Optimizer
meaning: In model training, the method that chooses parameter updates using information such as gradients.
example: An optimizer adjusts weights after gradients have been calculated.
context: This is the training meaning; software optimizers can also transform programs to improve execution.

name: Embedding
meaning: A representation of an item as a list of numbers that can capture useful relationships.
example: Words used in related contexts may have related embeddings.
context: Nearby embeddings do not prove equal meaning or factual truth.

name: Attention
meaning: A mechanism that combines information from different positions using weights calculated for the current input.
example: The words around bank can help shape its representation in river bank versus bank account.
context: Self-attention uses positions within the same sequence. It is not human awareness, and attention weights alone do not explain every answer.

name: Transformer
meaning: A neural-network design that combines attention with other transformations and information about sequence positions.
example: A text-generation Transformer can produce a continuation one token at a time.
context: Attention alone is not the complete architecture; multiple Transformer variants exist.

name: AI hallucination
meaning: A generated statement that sounds plausible but is false or unsupported.
example: An assistant invents a book title and presents it as a real source.
context: This is a description of unreliable output, not a claim that the model has a human sensory experience.

name: Retrieval-augmented generation
meaning: Finding relevant material and supplying it as context for a generated answer.
example: A support assistant retrieves a product guide before answering a setup question.
context: Retrieved material and citations still need checking; retrieval is not a guarantee of accuracy.

name: AI agent
meaning: A model-driven system that can repeatedly choose actions, use tools, inspect results, and decide what to do next.
example: An agent searches approved files, reads a result, then decides whether another search is needed.
context: The label does not guarantee autonomy or success. Permissions, stopping rules, and action receipts matter.

name: HTML
meaning: The markup language used to describe the structure and meaning of web content.

name: CSS
meaning: The language used to describe how web content is presented, including color, spacing, and layout.

name: Debugging
meaning: Investigating why software behaves unexpectedly, finding the cause, and checking a correction.
example: Inspect a changing total to find where the wrong amount was added.
context: A debugger is a tool that helps inspect running code; debugging is the investigation process.

name: Refactoring
meaning: Changing the internal structure of code while keeping its intended observable behavior the same.
example: Move repeated calculations into one function, then rerun the behavior checks.

name: Technical debt
meaning: Future maintenance work caused by design or implementation choices that make later changes harder.
example: A rushed duplicated calculation must later be changed in five places.
context: A metaphor used in planning. Not every imperfection is deliberate debt, and the cost is not automatically measurable.

name: Hotfix
meaning: A focused change released urgently to correct an important problem.
example: Release a small fix for a sign-in failure before the next planned feature release.
context: Urgency does not remove the need for testing, review, and a safe rollback plan.

name: Boilerplate
meaning: Repeated setup or structural code needed before the distinctive part of a task.
example: Several small programs may share the same configuration and startup structure.
context: Common developer shorthand. Repeated code may still be necessary; do not delete it merely because it is boilerplate.

name: Rubber-duck debugging
meaning: Explaining code or a problem step by step to help notice assumptions and mistakes.
example: Describe what every line should do, then compare that with what actually happens.
context: The listener can be another person, an object, or a written explanation. They need not solve the problem for you.

name: Yak shaving
meaning: Getting drawn into a chain of supporting tasks while trying to finish an original task.
example: Before fixing one test, you find yourself updating a tool, its configuration, and its documentation.
context: Some dependencies are necessary. The phrase is a prompt to reassess scope, not proof that the work is useless.

name: Bikeshedding
meaning: Spending disproportionate discussion time on an easy minor detail while more important questions remain unresolved.
example: A team debates a button’s exact shade for an hour before deciding whether the workflow works.
context: Use carefully: a detail that seems minor to one person may matter for accessibility or another user need.

name: LGTM
meaning: A short review comment meaning the reviewer thinks the proposed change looks acceptable.
example: A teammate writes LGTM after reviewing a small change.
context: It is not proof that tests passed or formal approval unless the team’s process gives it that meaning.

name: Pull request
meaning: A proposal on a code-hosting service to review and merge a set of changes into another branch.
example: Open a pull request so teammates can inspect and discuss a bug fix.
context: Pull request and merge request are common platform-specific names for similar review workflows. Opening one does not itself merge or deploy the change.

name: integer division
meaning: Division of integer operands that discards the fractional part toward zero.
context: C# and C++ foundation examples.

name: remainder operator
meaning: The % operator gives the remainder of integer division.
context: C# and C++ foundation examples.

name: game state
meaning: Values describing the current game situation, such as score and turns remaining.
example: score = 0 and turns = 2 describe this game before its loop starts.
context: C# and C++ foundation examples.

name: Java class
meaning: A declaration that groups data fields and methods for Java objects.
example: Our public class Main contains the main method.
context: Java25 core.

name: Java method
meaning: A named operation inside a class or interface. It can receive inputs and may return an answer.
example: nextAge(8) calls a static method with argument 8.
context: Java25 core.

name: Java Scanner
meaning: A Java reader that splits input into tokens and can read values such as integers.
example: hasNextInt checks a token before nextInt consumes it.
context: Java25 core.

name: Java int
meaning: A whole-number type that stores values from -2147483648 through 2147483647.
example: int tickets = 3; declares a numeric variable.
context: Java25 core.

name: C function
meaning: A named piece of work that can receive inputs and send a result back.
context: C17 core

name: C format string
meaning: Text with marks that tell printf how to display the supplied values. Each mark must match its value type.
context: C17 core

name: C character array
meaning: A fixed group of char storage units. A string stored there also needs room for its ending zero.
example: char name[6] can hold five input characters plus the string terminator.
context: C17 core

name: C pointer
meaning: A value that can refer to a location in memory. A null pointer refers to no object or function.
example: A successful fgets returns a pointer to its destination array.
context: C17 core

name: C header
meaning: A file included by source files to provide shared declarations and preprocessing information.
context: C17 core

name: Java boolean
meaning: A type with two possible values: true and false.
context: Java25 core.

name: C comparison result
meaning: A check of two values. These C comparisons give int 1 for true and int 0 for false.
example: seats >= 2 can select an if branch.
context: C17 core

name: println!
meaning: Show text or values, then start a new line.
context: Show the word inside the quotes, then start a new line.

name: let mut
meaning: Give a value a name and allow later changes through that name.
context: Give the score a name and allow its value to change.

name: Rust numeric expression
meaning: A piece of code that works out a number.
context: Read the old score and add two to it.

name: Rust if
meaning: Choose a path by checking whether a condition is true.
context: Ask whether the score is at least five.

name: Rust while
meaning: Repeat a block while its test is true. Check before each turn.
context: Check the count before every turn through the loop.

name: Rust return expression
meaning: The last expression can give a function its answer when it has no final semicolon.
context: Multiply the input by two and give that answer back.

name: echo
meaning: Show one or more values. Echo does not add a new line unless the text includes one.
context: Echo shows Moon. The backslash and n inside these quotes start a new line.

name: PHP variable
meaning: A name starting with a dollar sign that holds a value.
context: Put 8 in the variable that used to hold 3.

name: PHP arithmetic expression
meaning: Code that calculates a number from other values.
context: Work out the sum before storing it under the same name.

name: PHP if
meaning: Choose what to do by checking a condition.
context: Choose the first message if the score is five or more.

name: PHP while
meaning: Repeat the block while its condition stays true.
context: Only counts below three get a turn.

name: PHP function
meaning: A named set of instructions that can accept inputs and give back an answer.
context: Give the caller the result of multiplying the input by two.

name: puts
meaning: Show a value on its own line.
context: Show Moon and move to the next line.

name: Ruby local variable
meaning: A name that refers to a value within the part of the program where the name is available.
context: Give the name score the new value eight.

name: Ruby numeric expression
meaning: A piece of Ruby code that works out a number.
context: Work out five plus two before storing the answer.

name: Ruby if
meaning: Choose which path to take by checking a condition.
context: Use the Ready branch if the score meets the rule.

name: Ruby while
meaning: Repeat a block while its condition counts as true.
context: A count must be below three to enter the loop.

name: Ruby method
meaning: A named piece of behavior you can call on an object, with inputs when needed.
context: Ruby uses the last expression in this method as its answer.

name: R print
meaning: Display a value using R's usual printed form, which may include a position marker.
context: Print displays the value. The [1] in the output marks the position of the first item on that printed line.

meaning: Give the name on the left the value from the right.
